replies.author: @krstnenfu
replies.text:
@Africa107-was You are a victimizing, manipulating, cry baby. Nothing new for your type.

You did say it. Your original comment: “Then Napoleon Bonaparte asked the US to occupy Haiti on its behalf.” That is the claim that was corrected. You are now moving the goalposts.

Napoleon did **not** ask the United States to put down the Haitian rebellion with American troops or to occupy the island for him. He launched his own massive French expedition under Leclerc in 1801–1802. He sought diplomatic understandings with the US (and Britain) so French ships could sail and resupply without interference, because the French navy needed that neutrality/support to cross the Atlantic. American merchants sold supplies. That is ordinary wartime diplomacy, not a request for the US to suppress the revolt on France’s behalf.

Early in the 1790s revolt (under Washington), the US did give limited aid to French planters because of alliance obligations and Southern fears that a successful slave uprising could spread. Under Jefferson those fears continued—Southern slaveholders were genuinely alarmed by the Haitian example—but Jefferson’s policy was not to send US forces to fight for Napoleon. The Louisiana Purchase still happened because Napoleon’s expedition failed, he abandoned the Western Hemisphere project, and he needed money for European wars. That part of the history is not in dispute.

The rest of your reply simply repeats the same claims already addressed: the US occupied Haiti in 1915–1934 (true, after Haitian chaos), later dealt with the Duvaliers (true, Cold War realpolitik), and US rice later undercut Haitian farmers (true under tariff and subsidy policies). None of that proves a continuous American plot to “deliberately keep Haiti poor.” Haitian leaders, elites, and factions repeatedly chose predation, coups, and internal violence over building functional institutions. Blaming only outsiders while refusing to examine that record is the victimization you complained about.

I know people that live in Haiti. I watched a girl get cut to pieces and eaten a few weeks ago. Enough with your crybaby blaming and pointing fingers. Wakanda isn't real. You don't have any high trust functioning societies self-governed IN THE ENTIRE WORLD!

replies.author: @krstnenfu
replies.text:
@Africa107-was HAHA! Take your own advice and learn history for yourself. Wakanda isn't real.

Haiti was the first independent Black republic in the Western Hemisphere (declared 1804 after the slave revolt against France). That part is correct. Everything else is distorted or false.
Napoleon never asked the US to occupy Haiti. He sent his own large French army (under Leclerc) in 1802 to crush the revolt and restore control (and likely slavery). The expedition failed due to Haitian resistance, yellow fever, and war with Britain. The Louisiana Purchase happened because Napoleon abandoned his American ambitions after that defeat and needed cash—not because he asked the US to take over Haiti.

France did impose a massive indemnity in 1825 (initially 150 million francs, later reduced) as the price of recognizing Haitian independence. That debt was real and harmful for decades. It does not explain 200 years of continuous failure.

The US occupied Haiti from 1915–1934 after years of Haitian political chaos, assassinations, and debt defaults. It was heavy-handed, built some infrastructure, controlled finances, and left a centralized state that later dictators used. It was not continuous “exploitation ever since.”
Papa Doc and Baby Doc were Haitian dictators who ruled through terror (Tonton Macoutes) and theft. The US tolerated and aided them during the Cold War as anti-communists. When popular uprising forced Baby Doc out in 1986, the US provided the Air Force plane at his request (with French cooperation) to get him to France and avoid more bloodshed. France accepted him in exile; the US refused him permanent asylum. That is not evidence the US uniquely “propped them up” or kept Haiti poor.

Rice: Haiti reduced tariffs in the 1980s–90s under international pressure and its own government decisions. Cheap subsidized US rice (“Miami rice”) undercut local farmers. That hurt rural production. It is one factor among many—not proof the US (DEMOCRAT PARTY) deliberately “kept Haiti poor.”

Haiti’s poverty and dysfunction are not the result of perpetual US puppetry going back to Napoleon. Napoleon’s European wars, Russia campaign, and Waterloo (1815, not mid-19th century) are irrelevant to that claim. Haitian leaders and factions repeatedly chose predation, coups, and zero-sum violence instead of building functional institutions. External interference often made things worse, but it does not erase Haitian agency or the pattern of self-inflicted collapse.
